name: n8n
scope_notes: Covers n8n (Cloud and self-hosted). Public API is on Cloud Starter/Pro/Enterprise and all self-hosted editions (not free trial); key scopes, log streaming and token exchange are Enterprise; env-var controls apply only to self-hosted.

controls.name: N8N_PUBLIC_API_DISABLED
controls.what: Turns off the public REST API for the whole instance.

controls.name: API key scopes
controls.what: Limits a key to chosen resource:action scopes.
controls.setting: Settings > n8n API > Create an API key > Scopes

controls.name: API key expiration
controls.what: Key creator sets an expiration time.
controls.setting: Settings > n8n API > Create an API key > Expiration

controls.name: Delete API key
controls.setting: Settings > n8n API > Delete > Delete Forever

controls.name: Enable/Disable MCP access
controls.what: Turns the instance MCP server on or off; disabling disconnects every client.

controls.name: Per-workflow MCP access
controls.what: Only workflows marked Available in MCP can be read in full, run or edited.
controls.setting: Workflow settings > Available in MCP; Settings > Instance-level MCP > Workflows enabled

controls.name: Rotate MCP access token
controls.what: Generating a new token revokes the old one.
controls.setting: Settings > Instance-level MCP > Connect > API key tab

controls.name: Revoke access (connected clients)
controls.what: Disconnects an OAuth MCP client immediately.
controls.setting: Settings > Instance-level MCP > Connected clients > Revoke access

controls.name: Allowed callback URLs
controls.what: Restricts which redirect URLs can finish an MCP OAuth sign-in.
controls.setting: Settings > Instance-level MCP > Access > Allowed callback URLs

controls.name: allowedRoles (trusted key source)
controls.what: Restricts which roles token exchange may assign.

controls.name: Credential type policy
controls.what: Instance or project rules for which credential types are allowed.

controls.name: Allowed HTTP Request Domains
controls.what: Limits which domains a credential can be sent to from the HTTP Request node.
controls.setting: Credential modal > Allowed HTTP Request Domains

controls.name: N8N_TOKEN_EXCHANGE_ENABLED
controls.what: Token exchange is off unless this environment variable is true; the endpoint then returns 501. The preview flag N8N_ENV_FEAT_TOKEN_EXCHANGE must also be set to turn it on.
controls.setting: Environment variable N8N_TOKEN_EXCHANGE_ENABLED: leave unset or false to keep it off (Cloud: ask n8n support)

no_control.what: Scopes to limit a key are not available outside Enterprise; those keys have full account access.
No admin approval step for MCP OAuth clients; any signed-in user can approve one while MCP is on.
Removing a compromised signing key does not end already-issued tokens or sessions.
OAuth scope and resource in the exchange request are not enforced.

controls_unknown: Whether n8n API keys or MCP tokens are rejected when SSO is enforced or when a user is deleted
Any IP allowlist for API or MCP requests on n8n Cloud
Whether an admin can list or revoke other users' API keys or MCP API-key tokens
Whether 'no expiration' is an option for API keys, and default/maximum lifetime
Whether public API read calls (GET /workflows, /executions, /credentials) produce any audit event
Audit log retention (log streaming forwards events; retention is in the customer destination)

authentication.summary: Each user creates keys in Settings > n8n API. The key is sent in the X-N8N-API-KEY header to /api/v1 and acts as that user.

federation.details: Static key; no workload federation for API keys documented.

ip_restriction.boundary: No n8n-side IP allowlist for the API is documented; self-hosted operators can only restrict at their own network edge.

renewal.summary: Create a new key and delete the old one.

administration.summary: Self-hosted admins can turn off the whole public API with N8N_PUBLIC_API_DISABLED. Scopes only exist on Enterprise; other editions get full access.
administration.conditions: No per-user admin block or approval flow documented for Cloud.

usage.ui: Settings > Log Streaming > Add new destination > Events: Audit (n8n.audit), Workflow (n8n.workflow); filter on userId (Enterprise)

token_format.notes: Prefix not documented. Sent in X-N8N-API-KEY header.

log_sources.name: Log streaming (Audit group)
log_sources.notes: Enterprise. Destinations: syslog, webhook, Sentry. Retention depends on destination.

credential_id_fields.notes: Identifies the user, not the key. No key ID field documented.

lifecycle_events.notes: Display name in Settings > Log Streaming > Events.

anomaly_cues: User API created for an account that does not normally automate
Workflow created/updated/activated or Execution data revealed shortly after key creation

containment.steps: Delete the key in Settings > n8n API (as the key owner). On self-hosted, N8N_PUBLIC_API_DISABLED=true stops all key use.
containment.notes: Docs do not say whether deletion is immediate.

calls.reveals: Endpoints and operations the key can use

credentials.name: MCP access token (instance-level MCP, API key tab)

authentication.summary: n8n generates a personal access token per user for the instance MCP server, sent as Authorization: Bearer to the /mcp-server/http endpoint.

renewal.summary: Generating a new token revokes the previous one.

administration.summary: MCP is off until an owner/admin enables it; disabling it disconnects all clients. Self-hosted can remove the module or pin settings by env var. Only workflows explicitly enabled for MCP can be read in full or run.
administration.conditions: API-key clients do not appear in the Connected clients list, so admins cannot revoke them there.

inventory.details: API-key MCP clients do not appear in the Connected clients list; their tool calls show only in the n8n.audit.mcp.tool.called log with authType api_key (Enterprise log streaming).

inventory.ui: No list. Settings > Log Streaming: subscribe to n8n.audit.mcp; filter n8n.audit.mcp.tool.called on authType=api_key, group by userId (Settings > Instance-level MCP > Connected clients > View all lists only OAuth clients)

usage.ui: Settings > Log Streaming > Add new destination > Events: n8n.audit.mcp; filter authType=api_key and userId

reads.ui: Settings > Log Streaming > Events: n8n.audit.mcp; filter event n8n.audit.mcp.tool.called with authType=api_key; see toolName, workflowId

kill.ui: Token owner: Settings > Instance-level MCP > Connect > API key tab > generate new token (revokes old). Admin: Connection details > MCP status > Disable (revokes all clients)

credential_id_fields.notes: api_key for any non-OAuth bearer token.

anomaly_cues: authType=api_key tool calls from a user who normally uses OAuth

containment.steps: Owner rotates the token (revokes old). Admin can disable instance MCP, which revokes all clients.
containment.notes: Rotation revokes the previous token; no token creation event documented.

calls.reveals: Previews of all workflows the user can view

authentication.summary: An MCP client (Claude, ChatGPT, Cursor, etc.) runs an OAuth flow; the user approves it in n8n and the client gets the permissions granted at consent.

federation.details: User OAuth consent, not workload federation.

renewal.summary: Log docs mention the client's token refreshes; lifetimes are not documented.

administration.summary: Any signed-in user can approve a client while MCP is on. Owners/admins can restrict OAuth callback URLs (default allows any) and revoke clients for all users.

inventory.details: Settings > Instance-level MCP > Connected clients > View all, all-users view lists every connected OAuth client.

usage.ui: Settings > Log Streaming > Add new destination > Events: n8n.audit.mcp; filter authType=oauth, group by clientId

reads.ui: Settings > Log Streaming > Events: n8n.audit.mcp; filter event n8n.audit.mcp.tool.called with authType=oauth and clientId

anomaly_cues: New clientName not in approved list
Callback URL mode left at All callback URLs

containment.steps: Settings > Instance-level MCP > Connected clients > Revoke access (all-users view for others).

calls.reveals: Previews of every workflow the user can view
calls.log_notes: Log streaming is Enterprise only; MCP audit events from n8n 2.34.0.

credentials.name: Token exchange access token (OEM embedding, preview)

authentication.summary: A partner backend signs a short-lived JWT; n8n verifies it against trusted keys and returns a bearer access token (or a session cookie for iframe SSO).

federation.details: RFC 8693 exchange using static public keys or a JWKS URL in N8N_TOKEN_EXCHANGE_TRUSTED_KEYS. Requested scope is recorded but not enforced.

ip_restriction.boundary: Only per-IP rate limits on the exchange endpoint are documented.

lifetime.summary: Min of subject/actor JWT lifetime and N8N_TOKEN_EXCHANGE_MAX_TOKEN_TTL (default 15 min)

renewal.summary: Mint a new external JWT (jti is single-use) and exchange again.

administration.summary: Off unless N8N_ENV_FEAT_TOKEN_EXCHANGE and the per-flow toggles are set. allowedRoles limits which roles the JWT can assign.
administration.conditions: Enterprise; Cloud requires n8n support to enable.

sso.details: Issuance requires a JWT signed by the partner's trusted IdP/backend; n8n's own SSO settings are not described as applying.

inventory.details: No token list; issued tokens are visible only through n8n.audit.token-exchange.* audit events.

inventory.ui: No list. Settings > Log Streaming > Events: Audit > Token exchange succeeded (n8n.audit.token-exchange.succeeded)

disable.cli: Leave N8N_TOKEN_EXCHANGE_ENABLED unset or not true (endpoint returns 501); Cloud: ask n8n support

sso.cli: Set N8N_TOKEN_EXCHANGE_TRUSTED_KEYS to your IdP/backend key sources with issuer, expectedAudience and allowedRoles

usage.ui: Settings > Log Streaming > Add new destination > Events: n8n.audit.token-exchange.* (Enterprise)

credential_id_fields.notes: Scope and resource are recorded in audit events per the page.

containment.steps: Remove the trusted key entry; set N8N_TOKEN_EXCHANGE_ENABLED=false.
containment.notes: Issued tokens stay valid until expiry (default max 15 min).

calls.reveals: Workflows visible to the acting user

credentials.name: Stored credentials (third-party secrets held by n8n)

authentication.summary: Secrets for external services saved in n8n and used by workflow nodes. A compromised n8n account or API key can use them through workflows; the API does not return secret values.

ip_restriction.boundary: Allowed HTTP Request Domains limits where a credential can be sent from the HTTP Request node only; not a source-IP control.

renewal.summary: Rotate at the external service and update the credential.

administration.summary: Admins can set an instance or project credential type policy via the API.
administration.conditions: Plan for credential type policy not stated.

offboard.details: On user deletion the admin chooses to transfer the user's credentials to another user or delete them; the secret stays valid at the external service either way.

inventory.details: GET /api/v1/credentials lists all credentials on the instance for owner/admin.

usage.ui: Settings > Log Streaming > Events: Audit (User credentials created/shared/updated/deleted) and Workflow (n8n.workflow.*, by workflowId)

offboard.ui: Settings > Users > three-dot menu > Delete user > transfer or delete their credentials; then rotate the secret at the external service

anomaly_cues: Credential shared or transferred to a new project
New workflow using HTTP Request node with a credential set to All domains

containment.steps: Rotate the secret at the external service, then update or delete the n8n credential.

unknown: Whether credential use by workflows is logged per credential

calls.reveals: Credential names and types, not secrets
